To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

recyclers’ inclusion is a complex process that requires a continuous effort to achieve, that recyclers’ organisations are not homogeneous, and that the partnership needs to take into account recyclers’ organisations’ specificities and dynamics.
the recyclers’ perspective on the inclusive recycling project in Santiago de Chile shows that it is inclusive neither in its goals, nor in its process, nor in its outcomes.

recyclers perceive the project as a partnership in which they are not fully involved in the decision-making processes, but in which the project’s objectives and outcomes are aligned with their interests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which inclusive recycling can be considered inclusive for the recyclers.
how to make partnerships more inclusive, and how to assess their inclusiveness.
the extent to which a project aiming to promote the socioeconomic inclusion of recyclers in the waste sector is actually inclusive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inclusive recycling is not as inclusive as it sounds.
inclusive recycling is not inclusive enough, but that it can be.
the partnership in question is not inclusive in the way recyclers perceive it, but it is inclusive enough to be considered a successful partnership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partnership is not inclusive enough.
inclusive recycling is not inclusive, and that the inclusion of recyclers in cross-sector partnerships is a complex issue, which needs to be further studied and discussed.
inclusive recycling is not necessarily an inclusive process, and that the inclusion of the recyclers in the partnership is not enough to ensure their inclusion in the project itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to be more inclusive and effective, partnerships need to take into account recyclers’ needs and to be more flexible and adaptive in their implementation.
a more inclusive approach to inclusive recycling is needed.

, in order to be inclusive, cross-sector partnerships should be designed with an inclusive approach, which requires to take into account recyclers’ perspectives and to involve them in the project’s design and implementation, as well as to recognise their achievements and to acknowledge the local dynamics in which they are embedded.
